entities.summary: Marcus Furius Bibaculus was a Roman neoteric poet who flourished during the last century of the Republic. Born into a family of moderate means, he was educated in the traditional arts of rhetoric and poetry, and was heavily influenced by the works of Catullus and Propertius. His poetry, known for its lyricism and emotional depth, often explored themes of love, loss, and the human condition. Bibaculus's work was widely acclaimed by his contemporaries, including the poet and statesman Horace, who praised his 'beautiful and subtle verse'. Despite his literary success, Bibaculus's life was marked by personal turmoil, including a tumultuous marriage and a series of financial struggles. He died in 100 BCE, at the age of approximately 60, leaving behind a body of work that would be remembered for centuries to come. His poetry continues to be studied and admired today, offering a unique window into the culture and values of ancient Rome.
